MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #13
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which statement about 1,357 is correct? (1 mark)
   A. It is odd because it ends in 7
   B. It is even because it has an odd number of digits
   C. It is neither even nor odd
   D. It is even because it ends in 7

2. What is the total value of the digit 6 in 62,418? (1 mark)
   A. 6,000
   B. 60,000
   C. 6
   D. 600,000

3. Which of these is a factor of 28? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 7
   C. 6
   D. 3

4. In the number 24,613, the digit 4 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Hundreds
   B. Thousands
   C. Ones
   D. Tens

5. Estimate 5,382 + 3,617 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 9,010
   B. 9,099
   C. 8,990
   D. 9,000

6. Estimate 1,743 + 6,286 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 8,030
   B. 8,020
   C. 8,040
   D. 8,129

7. A library had 4,250 books and 1,875 were borrowed. How many books remained? (1 mark)
   A. 2,365 books
   B. 2,375 books
   C. 3,625 books
   D. 2,475 books

8. What is 27 × 20? (1 mark)
   A. 5,400
   B. 47
   C. 540
   D. 54

9. What is 48 × 20? (1 mark)
   A. 96
   B. 960
   C. 9,600
   D. 68

10. Estimate 33 × 27 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 9,000
   B. 1,000
   C. 900
   D. 800

11. What is 47 ÷ 5? (1 mark)
   A. 10 remainder 2
   B. 8 remainder 7
   C. 9 remainder 2
   D. 9 remainder 3

12. To check 32 × 3 = 96 using division we work out (1 mark)
   A. 96 − 32
   B. 32 ÷ 3
   C. 96 ÷ 32 × 3
   D. 96 ÷ 3

13. A rectangle is cut into 6 equal parts and 1 of the parts is shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 5/6
   B. 1/6
   C. 6/1
   D. 1/5

14. Beth writes another set of fractions. Which of these is a mixed fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 13/6
   B. 2/9
   C. 11/5
   D. 3 1/2

15. Change 2 7/10 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 27/10
   B. 28/10
   C. 20/10
   D. 9/10

16. Write 45/100 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 0.045
   B. 4.5
   C. 0.54
   D. 0.45

17. Write 5 7/100 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 5.07
   B. 5.007
   C. 5.7
   D. 57.0

18. Write 5/100 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 0.05
   B. 0.005
   C. 5.0
   D. 0.5

19. Which expression shows "3 times a number a"? (1 mark)
   A. 3a
   B. a − 3
   C. a ÷ 3
   D. a + 3

20. A rectangle has an area of 45 square units and 9 rows. How many columns does it have? (1 mark)
   A. 54
   B. 5
   C. 36
   D. 6

21. A rectangle has an area of 60 square units and 5 rows. How many columns does it have? (1 mark)
   A. 55
   B. 12
   C. 65
   D. 13

22. One layer of a cuboid has 24 blocks and there are 5 layers. What is the volume? (1 mark)
   A. 144 blocks
   B. 29 blocks
   C. 115 blocks
   D. 120 blocks

23. What is 5 kg − 1 1/2 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 3 3/4 kg
   B. 4 kg
   C. 3 1/2 kg
   D. 3 1/4 kg

24. What is 3 1/4 kg + 2 1/2 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 5 3/4 kg
   B. 5 1/2 kg
   C. 6 1/4 kg
   D. 6 kg

25. One unit costs Ksh 130. What is the cost of 6 loaves of bread? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 136
   B. Ksh 790
   C. Ksh 780
   D. Ksh 650

26. How many quarter turns make a half turn? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 2
   C. 3
   D. 1

27. Which everyday object has a face that is a circle? (1 mark)
   A. A door
   B. A coin
   C. A brick
   D. A roof end

28. A door has four straight sides and four square corners, with two long sides and two short sides. What shape is its face? (1 mark)
   A. Square
   B. Circle
   C. Rectangle
   D. Triangle

29. The table shows the vehicles that passed a school gate (10 vehicles): matatu 5, boda boda 2, bus 2, lorry 1. How many are NOT lorry? (1 mark)
   A. 10
   B. 9
   C. 11
   D. 1

30. The table shows the vehicles that passed a school gate (10 vehicles): matatu 5, boda boda 2, bus 2, lorry 1. What is the total of all the numbers? (1 mark)
   A. 12
   B. 11
   C. 9
   D. 10

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. A class has 30 pupils. Two fifths of them walk to school. How many pupils walk to school? (3 marks)

32. Change 3.4 m to centimetres. (2 marks)

33. Work out 4,000 − 1,236. Show how you regroup. (3 marks)

34. A tailor has 3 m 60 cm of cloth and uses 1 m 85 cm. How much cloth is left? (3 marks)

35. Divide 91 by 7 and check by multiplication. (3 marks)

36. Write 13.42 in expanded form and give the total value of the digit 4. (3 marks)

37. Wairimu had d shillings and spent 45 shillings. Write an expression for what she has left and find it when d = 100. (3 marks)

38. Start at 10,000 and subtract 1,500 each time. Write the first five numbers of the pattern. (3 marks)

39. Wafula has 20 goats. One fifth of them are brown. How many goats are brown? Show your working. (3 marks)

40. A shop earned Ksh 4,750 on Monday and Ksh 3,895 on Tuesday. How much did it earn on the two days? (3 marks)

41. Amina says the area of a rectangle with 4 rows and 6 columns is 10 because 4 + 6 = 10. Explain her mistake and give the correct area. (3 marks)

42. Show two different ways to make Ksh 50 using coins and notes. (2 marks)

43. Write 4, 6 and 9 as Roman numerals. (3 marks)

44. Explain what the 0 in 4.05 shows and say how 4.05 is different from 4.5. (3 marks)

45. A school uniform costs a shirt Ksh 650, shorts Ksh 800 and shoes Ksh 1,900. Find the total cost and the change from Ksh 5,000. (4 marks)

46. Explain why you should read a measuring jug at the same height as the water. (2 marks)

47. Simplify 2a + 5 + 3a + 1 and find its value when a = 4. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #13 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — It is odd because it ends in 7
   Look at the ones digit. 7 is odd, so 1,357 is odd.

2. B — 60,000
   The digit 6 is in the ten thousands place, so its total value is 6 × 10,000 = 60,000.

3. B — 7
   28 ÷ 7 = 4 with nothing left over, so 7 is a factor of 28. The others leave a remainder.

4. B — Thousands
   Counting from the right the places are ones, tens, hundreds, thousands and ten thousands. The digit 4 is in the thousands place.

5. D — 9,000
   5,382 rounds to 5,380 and 3,617 rounds to 3,620. 5,380 + 3,620 = 9,000.

6. A — 8,030
   1,743 rounds to 1,740 and 6,286 rounds to 6,290. 1,740 + 6,290 = 8,030.

7. B — 2,375 books
   Subtract 4,250 − 1,875 = 2,375. Check by adding: 2,375 + 1,875 = 4,250.

8. C — 540
   27 × 2 = 54, then × 10 gives 540.

9. B — 960
   48 × 2 = 96, then × 10 gives 960.

10. C — 900
   33 rounds to 30 and 27 rounds to 30. 30 × 30 = 900.

11. C — 9 remainder 2
   5 × 9 = 45 and 47 − 45 = 2. So 47 ÷ 5 = 9 remainder 2. Check: 9 × 5 + 2 = 47.

12. D — 96 ÷ 3
   Division undoes multiplication: 96 ÷ 3 = 32.

13. B — 1/6
   The whole has 6 equal parts and 1 are shaded, so 1/6 is shaded.

14. D — 3 1/2
   A mixed fraction has a whole number and a proper fraction, like 3 1/2.

15. A — 27/10
   2 × 10 = 20 and 20 + 7 = 27. The denominator stays 10, so the answer is 27/10.

16. D — 0.45
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 45/100 = 0.45.

17. A — 5.07
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 5 7/100 = 5.07.

18. A — 0.05
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 5/100 = 0.05.

19. A — 3a
   The key words tell us the operation. "3 times a number a" is written 3a.

20. B — 5
   Rows × columns = 45, so columns = 45 ÷ 9 = 5.

21. B — 12
   Rows × columns = 60, so columns = 60 ÷ 5 = 12.

22. D — 120 blocks
   Volume = blocks in one layer × layers = 24 × 5 = 120 blocks.

23. C — 3 1/2 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 5 kg − 1 1/2 kg = 3 1/2 kg.

24. A — 5 3/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 3 1/4 kg + 2 1/2 kg = 5 3/4 kg.

25. C — Ksh 780
   Cost = number × price = 6 × 130 = Ksh 780.

26. B — 2
   Two quarters make a half.

27. B — A coin
   A coin is round and flat, so its face is a circle.

28. C — Rectangle
   Opposite sides are equal but not all sides are equal, so it is a rectangle.

29. B — 9
   10 − 1 = 9.

30. D — 10
   Add all the numbers: 5 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 10.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: 12 pupils
   Working / marking points: 30 ÷ 5 = 6 (1 mark); 6 × 2 = 12 (1 mark); answer with unit (1 mark).

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: 340 cm
   Working / marking points: 3 m = 300 cm and 0.4 m = 40 cm (1 mark). 300 + 40 = 340 cm (1 mark).

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2,764
   Working / marking points: Borrow from the thousands so the number is 3 thousands 9 hundreds 9 tens 10 ones (1 mark). 10 − 6 = 4, 9 − 3 = 6, 9 − 2 = 7, 3 − 1 = 2 (1 mark). Answer 2,764 (1 mark).

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1 m 75 cm
   Working / marking points: 360 − 185 = 175 cm (2 marks); 175 cm = 1 m 75 cm (1 mark).

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: 13. Check: 13 × 7 = 91.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 7 × 13, 1 mark for 13, 1 mark for the check.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: 10 + 3 + 0.4 + 0.02. The total value of 4 is 0.4 (4 tenths).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 10 + 3, 1 mark for 0.4 + 0.02, 1 mark for the total value of 4.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: d − 45. When d = 100, she has 100 − 45 = 55 shillings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for d − 45, 1 mark for the substitution, 1 mark for 55 shillings.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: 10,000, 8,500, 7,000, 5,500, 4,000
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the correct rule and 2 marks for the numbers.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4 goats
   Working / marking points: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 (2 marks) and 1 × 4 = 4 goats (1 mark).

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 8,645
   Working / marking points: 4,750 + 3,895. Ones 5; tens 5 + 9 = 14 write 4 carry 1; hundreds 7 + 8 + 1 = 16 write 6 carry 1; thousands 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. 1 mark for setting up, 1 for regrouping, 1 for the answer with units.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: She added the rows and columns. Area is rows × columns = 4 × 6 = 24 square units.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying she added, 1 mark for saying multiply, 1 mark for 24.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: one Ksh 50 note; or five Ksh 10 coins; or two Ksh 20 coins and one Ksh 10 coin.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: IV, VI, IX
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each. IV is 5 − 1, VI is 5 + 1, IX is 10 − 1.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: The 0 shows that there are no tenths. 4.05 is 4 ones and 5 hundredths; 4.5 is 4 ones and 5 tenths, which is bigger.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning of zero, 1 mark for each correct reading.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Total Ksh 3,350; change Ksh 1,650
   Working / marking points: 650 + 800 + 1,900 = 3,350 (2 marks); 5,000 − 3,350 = 1,650 (2 marks).

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Looking from above or below makes the water level seem to be at a different mark, so the reading would be wrong.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying the reading can be wrong and 1 mark for the reason.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: 5a + 6. When a = 4, 5 × 4 + 6 = 26.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 5a, 1 mark for 6, 1 mark for replacing a, 1 mark for 26.
